text:
maria: FYI seeing repeated interface errdisable on ToR-17 (eu-west-2 rack-43) starting ~08:12 UTC. Egress TX errors and drops rising. A few dedicated-pool allocations started preempting.
liam: is it switch hw flapping or something upstream?
maria: looks like physical port flaps: syslog shows "%LINK-3-UPDOWN: Interface Gi1/0/17, changed state to down" multiple times. no BGP adjacency loss yet.
josh: impact: 6 allocations in dedicated-pool-eu observed >150ms tail p99, 3 preemptions. SLOs tripped.
oncall-bot: [ALERT] dedicated-pool-eu.egress_queue_p95 > threshold @08:16 UTC. Incident created: #incidents.
anya: can we route affected tenants through an egress fallback so they don't preempt? we have the fallback proxy but no automatic trigger from port events.
maria: suggestion: short-lived egress-guard on rack when port flaps detected. infra tags allocations via allocator-annotate, tag = "egress-guard:tor-17" and policy routes traffic to egress-fallback-gw for 5m. keeps jobs running with degraded bandwidth instead of preempting.
liam: sounds OK but need to preserve dedicated customer opt-outs and avoid billing surprises. 5m default fine. who owns the route change? netops?
netops: we can author a route-map that matches HW tag and redirects to fallback, but changing ToR config needs a maintenance window. alternative: egress proxy can pull allocation tags from control plane and accept reroutes without ToR change.
maria: infra path is preferable (no ToR edits). plan: 1) switch syslog -> cloudstream, 2) detector lambda parses flaps and emits event, 3) allocator-annotate service attaches tag "egress-guard=tor-17" to live allocations on that rack, 4) egress-proxy and router-policy observe tag and steer traffic. untag after TTL.
josh: fallback headroom in eu-west-2 ~25%. we should canary on low-priority tenants first.
liam: agree. propose canary: 3 test tenants for 10m starting 22:00 UTC, collect metrics (preemptions, p95/p99 tail, tx_drops).
anya: must respect Dedicated opt-out: allocations with annotation "dedicated:strict=true" should not be moved. default policy: allow soft reroute for bursty tenants.
sre-bot: runbook updated: "tor flapping -> egress-guard workflow". Play steps: detect -> notify netops -> apply tags -> monitor 10m -> remove tags -> postmortem if repeated.
oncall-bot: [UPDATE] incident #incidents assigned to @liam @maria @netops.
liam: action items: maria build detector + tests, anya validate allocator-annotate acceptance of tag, netops prepare proxy filter logic, josh reserve fallback headroom and schedule canary.
maria: I'll open a PR with lambda + parser and a test harness. quick repro to simulate syslog:
```
# emit switch syslog into cloudstream
aws kinesis put-record --stream ToR-syslog --data '{"host":"tor-17","facility":"local0","message":"%LINK-3-UPDOWN: Interface Gi1/0/17, changed state to down"}'
```
maria: demo command to tag allocations manually for tests:
```
infractl tag-allocs --rack tor-17 --add "egress-guard=tor-17" --ttl 300
```
liam: please add metric names: `infra.egress_guard.applied{tor="tor-17"}` and `infra.egress_guard.evicted`. emit billing tag `egress_guard=true` so cost dashboard can break out.
josh: I'll run the canary tonight 22:00 UTC and watch for preemptions/drop recovery. will report.
anya: Also add an opt-out check in allocator-annotate: skip tagging if `dedicated:strict=true`.
maria: noted. I'll include opt-out in PR. thanks. :thumbsup:
netops: we'll not touch ToR config until infra-only flow validated. standing by for verification.
liam: good work. update the incident and ops board when canary starts.
maria: closing thread for now, will paste PR + canary plan link when ready.
